### Saul Kills the Priests at Nob
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/saul-kills-the-priests-nob
Passage: 1 Samuel 22:14
Points:
- Saul's consuming paranoia blinded him to reality, causing him to view loyal servants as treasonous conspirators.
- Ahimelech aided David in good faith, completely unaware of the king's murderous hostility.
- Saul showed a total absence of the fear of God by ordering the massacre of the priests and the destruction of Nob.
- David demonstrated godly integrity by accepting responsibility for the tragedy and offering sanctuary to the surviving priest, Abiathar.
- Human depravity knows no limits when God gives people over to the unrestrained desires of their hearts.

### Day 29: 1 Samuel 22:11–23
Author: Beth Moore
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/plus/books/portraits-of-devotion/portraits-of-devotion-day-29-1-samuel-22-1123.html
Passage: 1 Samuel 22:17
Points:
- Saul's envy and hatred led to utter irreverence as he commanded the slaughter of innocent priests of the Lord.
- Saul's own guards showed greater godly restraint than the king by refusing to execute the priests.
- Saul and Doeg exemplified how toxic insecurity drives individuals to build themselves up by destroying others.
- David responded to the catastrophic news by casting himself upon God, remembering that God is good and will judge evil.
- In the face of unimaginable tragedy and unexplainable evil, believers must anchor their hope in God's faithfulness.
